ceiling_directive: Extend the higher-order interval to the full positive-density class in the regime q >= gamma by privately stabilizing the local density-weighted Gram, and prove an honest upper bound matching the ordinary gamma-smooth lower rate.
improvement_directive: Replace the uniform-design Lebesgue projector and globally sensitive quadratic Gram release with a private density-weighted, locally stabilized construction on P_full. Prove that it removes the N_priv^{-gamma/(gamma+2d)} term and matches the existing ordinary lower bound in at least the q >= gamma phase.
critique: The note proves a finite-sample private honest interval and a three-term expected-length upper bound only on the uniform-design attainable subclass, together with a valid but nonsharp full-class bracket. It proves no sharp minimax rate on either class: the attainable lower bound contains only the ordinary gamma-smooth terms, while the attainable upper has additional nuisance and private-Gram terms. The advertised phase diagram is therefore an achievability decomposition rather than a certified frontier, and the full-class beta-versus-gamma gap remains entirely open. The full-class endpoints largely lift inherited point-risk arguments to interval length and do not supply the missing nuisance-adaptive result. Unspecified envelope constants and the nonconstructive infinite-dimensional projections onto Holder balls also limit reproducibility and practical use, keeping the package below a field-level paper score.
